newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower as local money rates ease.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower as local money rates ease.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed lower against its U.S. counterpart on Wednesday amid active short-covering on U.S. dollars triggered by falling short-term interest rates, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.846 against Monday's T$27.812 close. The market was closed on Tuesday for banks' semiannual account settlement.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$238.5 million.
"As short-term interest rates are falling sharply today, U.S. dollar short-covering emerged actively," said one dealer.
The Taiwan dollar had risen in recent sessions due mainly to soaring short-term interest rates as investors scrambled for funds to put into the sizzling stock market.
At 0800 GMT, the overnight interbank rate was at 9.839 percent, still far outside the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5 percent but out of double digits for the first time since June 26.
The overnight rate had closed at 10.609 close on Monday.
Dealers said Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on July 1 had had little impact on Taiwan's money market.
For Thursday, a range of T$27.83-86 was seen.
